units.passage: Equity and access for all students
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account equity and access for all students.
units.why: 'Equity and access for all students' is a listed consideration for course policy; matches P51.

units.passage: If you are a student registered with DSS with an AI accommodation, please speak with me directly about your needs.
units.policy: Students registered with DSS who have an AI accommodation should speak with the instructor directly about their needs.
units.why: Example 1 text on Disability Support Services: 'If you are a student registered with DSS with an AI accommodation, please speak with me'; accommodation, P51.
units.fit_note: Mentions an AI accommodation specifically for DSS-registered students, which P51 only partly covers.

units.passage: Institutions should ensure that AI systems are compliant with accessibility standards and do not inadvertently disadvantage certain groups of students.
units.why: A separate duty in the same sentence: AI systems must not "disadvantage certain groups of students", an equity concern (P51).
units.fit_note: Fairness across student groups rather than cost or access.

units.passage: GenAI is a resource available to the university’s community, not a requirement for every academic or professional pursuit.
units.why: "AI is a university resource, not a technology mandate" and "not a requirement for every academic or professional pursuit": AI is optional. Nearest P51 (AI not required), though the passage is not about cost or access.
units.fit_note: Says AI is not required; the type centers on cost and equal access, which the passage does not mention. | Says AI is not required for every pursuit; it does not mention cost or access.

units.passage: Instructors should proactively investigate the accessibility and costs of AI tools before requiring students to use them
units.why: "Instructors should proactively investigate the accessibility and costs of AI tools before requiring students" is a duty on instructors about cost and access, so P51.

units.passage: To this end, instructors are encouraged to indicate this in their course descriptions and syllabi and include the monetary cost to students
units.policy: Instructors are encouraged to indicate in course descriptions and syllabi the monetary cost to students of required AI tools.
units.why: "instructors are encouraged to indicate this in their course descriptions and syllabi and include the monetary cost to students" asks for cost disclosure in syllabi. P51 (cost equity) fits best; P09 fits only partly because it concerns cost, not AI expectations.
units.fit_note: Asks for cost disclosure in syllabi, which P51 does not name explicitly. | Also a communication duty: state AI cost in the syllabus, not only keep access equitable.

units.passage: Make sure that a free version offers enough usage time and tools for students to complete the necessary work, with an ample margin for safety, before requiring it.
units.why: Library author notes free tiers are limited and advises checking a free version suffices "before requiring it"; labelled "This professor's opinion", advice on equitable access, so P51.
units.fit_note: Advice from a labelled opinion box, not the Senate guidelines themselves.

units.passage: Your students will appreciate it if you do the math to find them the best deal for the situation.
units.why: "Your students will appreciate it if you do the math to find them the best deal" advises instructors to compute subscription cost for students; cost equity advice (P51), labelled opinion.
units.fit_note: Opinion-box advice on subscription pricing.

units.passage: An absolute ban cuts off students from technologies which may help them succeed in your course, especially students requiring learning accommodations
units.why: "An absolute ban cuts off students from technologies which may help them succeed in your course, especially students requiring learning accommodations" argues against absolute bans on access grounds. P51 (accommodations) over P82 because the point is access, not enforceability.
units.fit_note: Opinion-box argument against absolute bans.

units.passage: The Library Al Access Program provides $150 mini-grants to help members of the Southern Miss campus community access an Al Pro tool for one semester.
units.why: "$150 mini-grants to help members ... access an Al Pro tool" provides funded access to AI tools, so P51 (equitable access), informs; it is a grant rather than a no-cost rule, so fit_note.
units.fit_note: A grant for access, with no statement that paid tools are not required. Access support is a competitive grant, not a guarantee of free access.

units.passage: Individuals should have the option to opt out without facing negative consequences.
units.why: 'Individuals should have the option to opt out without facing negative consequences' gives people an alternative to AI interaction. P51 covers 'alternatives exist'; P103 is about the right to know, which this does not state. It addresses everyone, should, and takes no side on AI use.
units.fit_note: Opt-out right when AI interacts with people, not cost or access. Adds a right to opt out without penalty, not only a right to know.

units.passage: Equity and access for all students
units.policy: In devising a generative AI policy, instructors should take equity and access for all students into account.
units.why: "Equity and access for all students" is a factor instructors should weigh in the policy; P51 covers equity and access, though the line names no concrete provision.
units.fit_note: Names equity and access as a factor only; no concrete provision such as free access or alternatives.

units.passage: Assignments will be designed with this in mind, and no student will be at a disadvantage for lack of access to AI technology.
units.why: 'Assignments will be designed with this in mind, and no student will be at a disadvantage for lack of access to AI technology' commits those who design assignments to keep access equitable (P51). 'will be designed' is a firm commitment, so it is must; it binds assignment designers, i.e. instructors, and applies before the course starts.

units.passage: Where the tools are recommended but not required, we suggest that instructors provide accommodations to students with reasonable objections.
units.policy: Where AI tools are recommended but not required, instructors should provide accommodations to students with reasonable objections.
units.why: "we suggest that instructors provide accommodations to students with reasonable objections" is an equity/alternative-access rule for recommended-but-not-required AI tools, P51, with should.

units.passage: If a student has ethical concerns about using generative AI tools, particularly if they are required to create an account with a tool that is not an institutionally approved resource, work with them to identify alternative ways to engage with the assignment.
units.why: "work with them to identify alternative ways to engage with the assignment" offers alternatives to students with ethical objections, so P51.

units.passage: Conducting manual or traditional research instead of using AI for ideation or content generation. • Partner with classmates who are comfortable using AI tools (if collaborative work is allowed). • Using public domain or open-access resources instead of proprietary AI tools.
units.why: "Conducting manual or traditional research instead of using AI" is one listed non-AI route for students who object, so P51.

units.passage: any requirement should account for access, cost, privacy, data security, intellectual property, and account creation
units.why: 'the university does not currently provide a single institutionally supported generative AI platform' and requirements 'should account for access, cost' - an access and cost caution, P51.
units.fit_note: Also lists privacy, security, IP and account creation. / Also lists privacy, data security, IP and account creation as factors.

units.passage: Students should not be required to purchase a subscription
units.why: 'Students should not be required to purchase a subscription unless it is clearly identified in the syllabus as required course material' is a no-paid-tool rule, P51.
units.fit_note: Exception: when a purchase is identified in the syllabus as required course material tied to outcomes.

units.passage: offer an alternative when a student cannot reasonably access or use the selected tool
units.why: Faculty should 'offer an alternative when a student cannot reasonably access or use the selected tool', an equity and access provision, P51.

units.passage: Equity issues may arise for students without consistent access to AI or paid subscriptions to AI applications
units.why: 'Equity issues may arise for students without consistent access to AI or paid subscriptions' names an access gap, P51.

units.passage: Equity issues may arise for students without consistent access to AI or paid subscriptions to AI applications
units.why: 'Equity issues may arise for students without consistent access to AI or paid subscriptions' names an access gap, P51.

units.passage: You will be informed about what data (if any) is shared, provided, or stored when we use any AI tool in the classroom—and you can opt out.
units.why: 'and you can opt out' gives students the right to opt out of AI tool use involving their data in class; a choice guarantee, nearest P51 (AI optional, alternatives) though the opt-out is about data.
units.fit_note: Opt-out concerns instructor-chosen AI tools that process student data, not student AI use. Opt-out concerns student data in instructor-used AI tools, not cost or access to student AI tools.

units.passage: If you choose not to use AI in your learning process, that is perfectly acceptable.
units.why: 'If you choose not to use AI in your learning process, that is perfectly acceptable' makes AI optional with no penalty; P51 (AI not required).
units.fit_note: Frames choosing not to use AI as acceptable rather than addressing cost or accommodations.

units.passage: If you would rather not use AI, that is perfectly acceptable.
units.why: 'the use of AI remains optional. If you would rather not use AI, that is perfectly acceptable' is the optional variant of required assignments; students may opt out, P51.
units.fit_note: Protects the choice not to use AI on a required-AI assignment, not cost or access.

units.passage: the use of AI remains optional. If you would rather not use AI, that is perfectly acceptable. Let me know, and accommodations or alternative assignments can be made.
units.why: "the use of AI remains optional" with "accommodations or alternative assignments" preserves choice for required-AI assignments; P51.

units.passage: When making these determinations, instructors should consider student access and equity, and they should remain mindful of privacy, ethical, and societal considerations.
units.why: Instructors "should consider student access and equity" when setting AI rules, P51.
units.fit_note: Also asks instructors to be mindful of privacy and ethical considerations.

units.passage: Faculty should ensure that all students can access digital tools if assignments require them. While many options are free, group projects or shared resources can help minimize access and disparity issues.
units.why: "Faculty should ensure that all students can access digital tools if assignments require them" is an equity duty on instructors, P51, should.

units.passage: A clear explanation should be provided in courses regarding available AI resources and (if any) costs
units.why: 'A clear explanation should be provided in courses regarding available AI resources and (if any) costs' asks courses to say what AI resources exist and what they cost: P51 (equitable access).

units.passage: The same AI resources should be available to all students.
units.why: 'The same AI resources should be available to all students' is an equal-access rule: P51.

units.passage: Faculty and staff should strive to provide alternative methods of engagement for students and employees who may have limited access to AI technologies.
units.why: "Faculty and staff should strive to provide alternative methods of engagement for students and employees who may have limited access to AI technologies" is a duty on instructors to arrange equitable alternatives, P51, should, set while designing the course.

units.passage: Please be aware that most Gen-AI tools not licensed by UVA require users to create an account using a cell phone number or entering other personal information. For this reason, students should not be required to create accounts for these tools.
units.why: "Students should not be required to create accounts" for unlicensed tools because they collect phone numbers or personal data; an access rule (P51) with a privacy motive.
units.fit_note: Reason given is personal-information privacy rather than cost. Limits what instructors can require, to protect students' personal data.

units.passage: If you design an assignment that involves students uploading their original work into a Gen-AI tool, you must provide alternative ways to complete the assignment.
units.why: "You must provide alternative ways to complete the assignment" when students must upload original work; an alternatives rule (P51).
units.fit_note: Alternative is required for privacy and IP reasons, not cost.

units.passage: Instructors may not require students to create an account with a non-UVA Gen-AI tool if — as in all or nearly all cases — creating the account requires sharing a phone number or other personal information.
units.why: "Instructors may not require students to create an account with a non-UVA Gen-AI tool" protects personal information; access rule (P51).
units.fit_note: Reason is personal information, not cost.

units.passage: Verify if the Gen AI resources are accessible and freely available for all students, to ensure equitable access.
units.why: "Verify if the Gen AI resources are accessible and freely available for all students, to ensure equitable access" is an equity and cost rule, so P51.

units.passage: Virginia Tech’s AI integration strategy prioritizes ensuring that all advancements bridge rather than exacerbate existing digital divides within the university community.
units.why: The strategy 'prioritizes ensuring that all advancements bridge rather than exacerbate existing digital divides' (P51).

units.passage: Several responses also raised concerns about fairness, especially when students have differing levels of access to AI tools
units.why: 'concerns about fairness, especially when students have differing levels of access to AI tools' reports an equity concern, P51.

units.passage: William & Mary also prioritizes inclusivity and fairness in its AI strategy – providing equitable access to AI resources and addressing bias – so that all members of the community can benefit
units.why: 'providing equitable access to AI resources and addressing bias' states fairness as a strategic priority (P51); admin, general, informs.

units.passage: To expand universal access to advanced AI tools and literacy programs, particularly for incoming students, to address equity gaps
units.why: Goal 'To expand universal access to advanced AI tools and literacy programs, particularly for incoming students, to address equity gaps' is access/equity (P51); admin, general, should.

units.passage: As with other emerging technologies, students from certain socioeconomic backgrounds may find themselves at a greater disadva ntage if their high schools and home experiences afforded them far less exposure and preparedness in using and experiencing AI
units.why: 'students from certain socioeconomic backgrounds may find themselves at a greater disadvantage' names unequal preparation as an equity issue (P51); informs.

units.passage: AI access: Most leading closed-source AI labs charge users for unlimited (or, in some cases, any) access to the highest-performing frontier models. The costs involved may be substantial: Students able to bear these expenses may reap significant educational and prof essional advantages
units.why: 'Most leading closed-source AI labs charge users for unlimited ... access'; 'Students able to bear these expenses may reap significant educational and professional advantages' names cost as an equity problem (P51); informs.

units.passage: A first step toward equitable AI at W&M would be to provide subscription-level access to one or more frontier models (e.g.
units.why: 'A first step toward equitable AI at W&M would be to provide subscription-level access to one or more frontier models' proposes free access (P51); admin, before-course, should.

units.passage: right now, some students at our university receive excellent instruction in functional and critical AI literacy, while others receive little or none. This inconsistency is more than a curricular gap; it’s an equity i ssue
units.why: 'right now, some students at our university receive excellent instruction in functional and critical AI literacy, while others receive little or none ... an equity issue' (P51); informs.
units.fit_note: Inequity of AI instruction rather than of AI tool access.

units.passage: AI literacy initiatives must be accessible to all students, not just those in tech -focused majors. This means offering multiple entry points into the material—before, during, and near the end of a student’s undergraduate journey—and ensuring content is inclusive and responsive to diverse needs
units.why: 'AI literacy initiatives must be accessible to all students, not just those in tech-focused majors' (P51 equal access); admin, general, must.
units.fit_note: About accessibility of AI-literacy programming across majors, not cost of AI tools.

units.passage: Financial equity is another concern; some students can afford premium subscriptions while others cannot
units.why: 'some students can afford premium subscriptions while others cannot' names cost-based inequity, which is P51's equity concern.

units.passage: To promote equity, UW–Madison provides no-cost access to several generative AI tools
units.why: 'provides no-cost access to several generative AI tools' is a university commitment to free access, framed 'to promote equity', so P51 (free access provided); it is also an institution-wide licensed tool offer (P92), which I did not choose because the stated point is equity.
units.fit_note: Also states that the university provides licensed tools institution-wide (P92).
